f75c84e0-aaf1-4262-9d61-ca4b6f1e672a@nin.why: The 49ers are off to a 2-0 start, outscoring both the Rams and Dolphins by big margins and sitting atop the NFC West. Arizona is a division rival that just lost badly to Seattle, so this is a good chance for San Francisco to build an early cushion in the division standings. It is only week three, so nothing is clinched or lost here, but a win would keep the 49ers unbeaten and add to their divisional tiebreaker edge.
f75c84e0-aaf1-4262-9d61-ca4b6f1e672a@nin.know: A division game means these two teams share the NFC West and play twice a year; those results matter extra later for tiebreakers and who wins the division. Watch running back Christian McCaffrey, who just reached 100 career touchdowns and is a focal point of the offense, and quarterback Brock Purdy, who has been sharp and mistake-free through two games.

75b7b5e8-6b02-4eee-a2ca-0ce91d9bc037@ufc.why: The main event pits ranked bantamweights, with rising prospect Raul Rosas Jr. (#12) facing veteran black belt Raoni Barcelos (#13); the matchup will massively impact both men's bantamweight trajectories. Elsewhere, ranked contenders Norma Dumont (#4) and Ailin Perez (#5) clash in a heated Brazil-Argentina rivalry, and with both athletes positioned inside the top five, the winner could take a significant step toward a future title opportunity.
75b7b5e8-6b02-4eee-a2ca-0ce91d9bc037@ufc.know: Rosas Jr. is a 21-year-old prospect currently on a five-fight win streak, having most recently beaten veteran Rob Font via unanimous decision at UFC 326, a card not on this calendar. Barcelos, by contrast, is a 39-year-old combat sports veteran who has also won five straight, using jiu-jitsu grappling. Fighters are ranked #1-15 below the champion; climbing that ladder by beating other ranked names is how title shots get earned.
